summary: Radar, 2026-10-30 15:00 UTC. The biggest signal this cycle is Lilly's topline TRANSCEND-T2D-2 result, retatrutide versus semaglutide 2 mg in type 2 diabetes. It is covered by about 30 outlets (Reuters, STAT, USA Today, ABC, Medscape), and a second wave is still arriving on 10-30 (Medscape, EMJ, FOX5). It does NOT qualify for Lane C. The first report was Lilly's release at 10:45 GMT on 10-28, about 52 h ago, which is past the 48 h rule. It also has no tirzepatide arm, and it is open-label and not yet peer-reviewed. Use it as the 13:00 retatrutide Short ('what's confirmed?' with a loop ending). Use the one-trial-per-week slot here and fold the new dysesthesia (skin-sensation) signal into it. Long-form stays on the Lane A order. Stopping tirzepatide goes next: SURMOUNT-4, refreshed by the 10-29 Diabetes Obes Metab semaglutide persistence cohort. Then protein, hair loss, bones and muscle, and plateau. The best new body-worry Short is thyroid: a new scoping review (10-27) on how thyroid ultrasound monitoring may inflate cancer detection on GLP-1 medicines, plus a papillary thyroid narrative review. It's a calm, honest-uncertainty piece with the MTC/MEN2 boxed-warning line. Plan ahead for ObesityWeek, 14–17 Nov in Washington DC. Novo has 26 abstracts there, including REDEFINE 9 (low-dose CagriSema, 21.0% vs 2.0% placebo at 68 weeks) and real-world Wegovy pill data on food-related thoughts. CagriSema's FDA decision window (Q4 2026) is open, so watch daily for a Lane C trigger. Seasonal: Thanksgiving Shorts and Reels peak 20–27 Nov. Rejected: online/compounded tirzepatide 'where to buy' and price pieces (Forbes, Business Insider press release). Cost and coverage news (employer plans dropping coverage, open enrollment) is banned by the playbook. Notes: PubMed abstract pages and Lilly's investor page blocked fetches, so the scriptwriter must confirm exact numbers from the PubMed records before writing. Retatrutide numbers were cross-checked across HCPLive, AJMC, 2 Minute Medicine and Medscape. I couldn't count YouTube competition directly. Search showed news coverage only and no dominant explainer video yet, so competition levels are estimates.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide vs semaglutide 2 mg in type 2 diabetes: TRANSCEND-T2D-2 topline (Lilly, Oct 28, 2026). About 1,300 adults with T2D on metformin ± SGLT2 inhibitor, randomized 2:2:1, open-label, 80 weeks. A1C down 2.2 points (12 mg) vs 1.8 (semaglutide 2 mg). Weight down 19.5% (9 mg) and 20.9% (12 mg) vs 9.4%
candidates.angle: 'Retatrutide vs Ozempic: what's actually confirmed?' Headlines say 'double the weight loss'. Show what that means and what it doesn't. Separate arms with exact numbers, adults with type 2 diabetes only, open-label, topline and not yet peer-reviewed, not approved (Lilly plans to file Q1 2027). Add the new detail most headlines skipped: dysesthesia (unusual skin sensations) in 4.8% and 6.5% vs 2.7%, and stopping because of side effects in 4.8% and 7.9% vs 2.7%. GI rates are similar across arms. Loop ending back to the 'double' headline. Short only: past the 48 h Lane C window (first report 10-28 10:45 GMT) and no tirzepatide arm. Uses this week's single-trial Short slot.
candidates.predicted_peak: 0–4 days (news peak passed 10-28/29; search tail runs about 2 weeks)
candidates.why_now: Multi-source spike across wire, trade and consumer TV outlets on 10-28 to 10-30 (Reuters, STAT, USA Today, ABC, NY Post, Medscape 10-30, EMJ 10-30). Retatrutide Shorts are our best Short lane (268, 202, 120) when they carry new Phase 3 data with a 'what's confirmed?' angle. Most coverage repeats 'double Ozempic' without the population, the open-label design or the dysesthesia signal.

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 (783 began the lead-in; 335 vs 335 randomized at week 36; +14.0% regain from week 36 to 88 on placebo), refreshed by the new population cohort on early treatment trajectory and long-term persistence with semaglutide (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 29, 2026)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, next in the playbook order. Open on a 'you' scenario: you've reached your goal and wonder if you can stop. First sentence answers: in the main trial, most people who switched to placebo regained a large share of the weight, and those who stayed on kept losing. Then cover what the new persistence data says about how many people stop early, why, and what helps keep results going (protein, strength training, follow-up with your prescriber). Must include 'don't stop or change your medicine on your own'.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and thyroid cancer: honest uncertainty. New scoping review on thyroid monitoring and how it may inflate cancer detection with GLP-1 medicines (Diabetes Res Clin Pract, Oct 27, 2026), plus a papillary thyroid carcinoma narrative review (J Clin Med, Oct 11)
candidates.angle: 08:00 body-worry Short: 'Does tirzepatide cause thyroid cancer? What we know.' Calm and honest. Large cohort data hasn't shown a clear link. Early rises in diagnoses may partly reflect more thyroid scans finding nodules that were already there (detection). The boxed warning comes from rodent studies and applies to people with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN2. Tell your prescriber about lumps, hoarseness or trouble swallowing. No reassurance beyond what the evidence supports.

candidates.topic: Does tirzepatide affect mood? New review of neuropsychiatric safety of GLP-1 RAs and tirzepatide (Rambam Maimonides Med J, Oct 26, 2026), a semaglutide panic-attack pharmacovigilance study testing 'notoriety bias' (Pharmacoepidemiol Drug Saf, Nov 2026), and the Medicare T2D neuropsychiatric cohort (Oct 25)
candidates.angle: 08:00 honest-uncertainty Short. Large studies so far haven't shown a clear increase in suicidal thoughts or depression. Report-based signals (like panic attacks) can rise when media attention rises (notoriety bias), which is not proof. Any mood change is worth telling your prescriber about right away. Compassionate tone, no self-harm detail, and point to crisis lines (988 US, Samaritans UK) where relevant.
candidates.why_now: Three new papers within a week on a high-anxiety question people search for. Few creators have covered the notoriety-bias nuance.
